title: HOME – Pilot project to implement a low-threshold psychological intervention called “Problem Management Plus (PM+)” for refugees in Bremen
summary:
Refugees may have a high need for psychosocial support and may show symptoms of mental health problems resulting from their flight and traumatic experiences in their country of origin. However, the majority of those who show signs of psychological distress and who need help do not receive the care they need. Reasons for that range from stigma and language barriers to limited access to appropriate care. The “Problem Management Plus” (PM+) intervention developed by the World Health Organization is a low intensity psychological intervention that aims to reduce psychological distress among populations exposed to adversities. What makes PM+ unique is that it is delivered by trained lay people in the participant's native language. This approach may facilitate access to care and builds trust in the intervention. PM+ has been thoroughly assessed in numerous projects around the world, including among refugee populations, and the results confirm its effectiveness. In Germany, however, no sustained implementation of PM+ has yet taken place.
The HOME project aims to implement the program PM+ in Bremen and to gain a better understanding of how it can be optimized and adapted to the local context. Another goal of the project is to develop guidelines that can serve as basis for introducing PM+ in other regions of Germany.
conditions: Common mental health problems such as depression and anxiety disorders

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	residing in Bremen
•	aged 18 years and above
•	moderate to high levels of psychological distress (K-10 score ≥ 15)
•	speaks a language covered by the lay helpers
•	refugees and asylum seekers including persons with a temporary residence permit or a residence permit under Sections 22, 23, 24, 25.1, and 25.2
Exclusion criteria:
Presence of a current problem requiring different treatment: acute suicidal tendencies, severe cognitive impairment, acute neurological conditions or severe mental disorders (e.g., psychotic or substance-abuse disorders) or ongoing outpatient or partially inpatient psychotherapy
